etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English red, from Old English rēad, from Proto-West Germanic *raud, from Proto-Germanic *raudaz from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rowdʰós, from the root *h₁rewdʰ-.

definitions.definition: Of a red hue.

quote.citation: c. 1596–1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Second Part of Henry the Fourth, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene iv]:
quote.text: Your colour, I warrant you, is as red as any rose.

quote.citation: 1954 July 29, J.R.R. Tolkien, “I: A Long-Expected Party”, in The Fellowship of the Ring (The Lord of the Rings; 1), →ISBN:
quote.text: The flowers glowed red and golden: snapdragons and sunflowers, and nasturtians trailing all over the turf walls and peeping in at the round windows.

definitions.definition: (of hair) Having an orange-brown or orange-blond colour; ginger.
(of the skin) Having a redder hue than usual due to embarrassment, anger, sunburn, etc.; flushed.

quote.citation: 1982, Douglas Adams, Life, the Universe and Everything, page 23:
quote.text: [T]he sun was shining on a happy crowd. It shone on white hats and red faces. It shone on ice lollies and melted them.

definitions.definition: (of a dog or its coat) Having a brown color.
(card games, of a card) Of the hearts or diamonds suits. Compare black (“of the spades or clubs suits”)
Left-wing parties and movements, chiefly socialist or communist, including the U.K. Labour party and the Social Democratic Party of Germany.
(US politics) The U.S. Republican Party. [21st c.]
(politics, often capitalized) Supportive of, related to, or dominated by a political party or movement represented by the color red:
(chiefly derogatory, offensive) Amerind; relating to Amerindians or First Nations

quote.text: All my friends are Indians / All my friends are brown and red

definitions.definition: (astronomy) Of the lower-frequency region of the (typically visible) part of the electromagnetic spectrum which is relevant in the specific observation.
(particle physics) Of a red color charge.
(countable and uncountable) The colour of the setting sun; the colour which is evoked by the longest visible wavelengths (between about 625–740 nm), and a primary additive colour.
(countable) A revolutionary socialist or (most commonly) a Communist; (usually capitalized) a Bolshevik, a supporter of the Bolsheviks in the Russian Civil War.
(countable, snooker) One of the 15 red balls used in snooker, distinguished from the colours.
(countable and uncountable) Red wine.

quote.citation: 1977 September, Billy Joel (lyrics and music), “Scenes from an Italian Restaurant”, in The Stranger:
quote.text: A bottle of red, a bottle of white / It all depends upon your appetite / I'll meet you any time you want / in our Italian restaurant.
He produced a wine key from his jacket pocket and effortlessly removed the cork from the bottle of red.

quote.citation: 2008 January–February, “70 Ways to Improve Every Day of the Week”, in Men's Health, volume 23, number 1, →ISSN, page 135:
quote.text: 59 sneak in some red Smuggle a bottle of wine, two glasses, and a corkscrew into a long matinee. Red wine is rich in life-extending antioxidants, and the caper will add zest even to a bad movie.

definitions.definition: (countable) Any of several varieties of ale which are brewed with red or kilned malt, giving the beer a red colour.

quote.citation: 2012 June 5, Howard Stelzer, Beer Cocktails: 50 Superbly Crafted Cocktails that Liven Up Your Lagers and Ales, Harvard Common Press, →ISBN:
quote.text: American reds and doppelbocks are heavy lagers as well. It really comes down to how the beer was made. Beyond that, brewers are immensely creative and have developed styles of both ale and lager that run a wide range of attributes.

quote.citation: 2016 April 1, Lonely Planet, Helena Smith, Andy Symington, Donna Wheeler, Lonely Planet Belgium & Luxembourg, Lonely Planet, →ISBN:
quote.text: No other country has a brewing tradition as richly diverse as that of Belgium, with beers ranging from pleasant pale lagers to wild, winelike Flemish reds and lambics.

definitions.definition: (countable, informal, Australia) A red kangaroo.
(countable, informal, UK, birdwatching) A redshank.
(derogatory, offensive) An American Indian.
(slang) The drug secobarbital; a capsule of this drug.

quote.citation: 1970, “Truckin'”, in American Beauty, performed by Grateful Dead:
quote.text: What in the world ever became of sweet Jane? / She lost her sparkle, you know she isn't the same / Livin' on reds, vitamin C, and cocaine

quote.citation: 1971, Hunter S. Thompson, Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas, Harper Perennial, published 2005, page 202:
quote.text: The big market, these days, is in Downers. Reds and smack—Seconal and heroin—and a hellbroth of bad domestic grass sprayed with everything from arsenic to horse tranquillizers.

quote.citation: 1998, Jeffery Deaver, The Coffin Dancer, New York, NY: Pocket Books, published 2021, →ISBN, page 285:
quote.text: “Whatchu got, man?” / “Reds, bennies, dexies, yellow jackets, demmies.” / “Yeah, demmies're good shit, man. I pay you. Fuck. I got money. I'm hurting inside. Got beat up. Where my money?”

definitions.definition: (informal) A red light (a traffic signal)

quote.citation: 1974, Tom Waits (lyrics and music), “(Looking for) The Heart of Saturday Night”, in The Heart of Saturday Night‎[2]:
quote.text: Stopping on the red, you're going on the green / Cause tonight will be like nothing you've ever seen / And you're barreling down the boulevard / You're looking for the heart of Saturday night

definitions.definition: (Ireland, UK, beverages, informal) Red lemonade
(particle physics) One of the three color charges for quarks.
(US, colloquial, uncountable) Chili con carne (usually in the phrase "bowl of red").

quote.text: Houston visited a home in an early pioneer settlement where he was offered a bowl of red. Houston eagerly took his first large spoonful. His eyes watering, he spat out his bite  […]

definitions.definition: (informal) The redfish or red drum, Sciaenops ocellatus, a fish with reddish fins and scales.

quote.citation: 2013 November, Catch Cormier, “Sightcasting for redfish”, in Louisiana Sportsman‎[3]:
quote.text: The species Sciaenops ocellatus certainly isn’t lacking for nicknames. […]  Clear water also favors sightcasting. Against the dark background of marsh mud, a red will appear like a pumpkin — big, orange and round.

definitions.definition: (slang, uncountable) Tomato ketchup.

quote.citation: 2016, Jon Bounds, Danny Smith, Pier Review: A Road Trip in Search of the Great British Seaside:
quote.text: I squeeze some red out over my chips and feel guilty. Nothing is as English as Heinz ketchup in the sauce game, except perhaps HP.

definitions.definition: (archaic) simple past and past participle of rede
